description: BLIP image captioning on CPU, monitored with Prometheus + node_exporter. Read top to bottom: health → throughput & latency → errors & clients → app resources → host resources. Shaded bands = bulk ZIP jobs.

panels.title: 1 · Health at a glance — is everything up and working?

panels.description:
Is the Streamlit captioning app reachable by Prometheus?

Source: Prometheus' built-in `up` series for job caption_app (1 = last scrape succeeded, 0 = failed). Green ✓ UP / red ✗ DOWN; the text carries the meaning, not the colour alone.

PromQL drafted with AI (Claude); prompt and hand-worked logic in AI_PROMPTS.md.
panels.title: App status

panels.description:
Is the system-metrics exporter reachable?

Source: `up{job="node"}`. If this is DOWN, the System rows below go blank.

PromQL drafted with AI (Claude); prompt and hand-worked logic in AI_PROMPTS.md.
panels.title: node_exporter status

panels.description:
Is the BLIP model loaded and ready to caption, and which model is it?

Joins the gauge `imgcap_model_loaded` (1/0) with the Info metric `imgcap_build_info` to show the model name as the label.

PromQL drafted with AI (Claude); prompt and hand-worked logic in AI_PROMPTS.md.
panels.title: Model

panels.description:
How long the app process has been running. A reset to ~0 means it restarted or crashed.

Computed as now − `process_start_time_seconds` (exported automatically by prometheus_client).

PromQL drafted with AI (Claude); prompt and hand-worked logic in AI_PROMPTS.md.
panels.title: App uptime

panels.description:
Current work in flight.

• Active requests: gauge `imgcap_active_requests` summed over modes (track_inprogress).
• Active sessions: browser sessions seen in the last 5 min (`imgcap_active_sessions`).
• Bulk queue: images left in the running ZIP job (`imgcap_bulk_queue_remaining`).

PromQL drafted with AI (Claude); prompt and hand-worked logic in AI_PROMPTS.md.
panels.title: Load right now

panels.description:
Share of images that failed (corrupt, too large, inference error) over the dashboard's selected time range.

failed ÷ all images from `imgcap_images_processed_total`. Example: 1 failed of 40 → 2.5%.
Green < 5% · amber 5–20% · red > 20% (matches the HighImageFailureRate alert).

PromQL drafted with AI (Claude); prompt and hand-worked logic in AI_PROMPTS.md.
panels.title: Image failure rate
2 · Throughput & latency — how much work, how fast?

panels.description:
How much work the app is doing. Solid lines = images captioned per second; dashed = requests per second. In single mode they match (1 request = 1 image); in bulk mode one request carries many images, so the solid line sits far above the dashed one. Colour = mode (blue single, orange bulk).

X axis: time. Y axis: events per second, linear scale. rate(counter[1m]) = increase over the last minute ÷ 60.

PromQL drafted with AI (Claude); prompt and hand-worked logic in AI_PROMPTS.md.
panels.title: Throughput — images and requests per second

panels.description:
How long captioning takes. p50 = typical image, p95/p99 = slow tail, from the `imgcap_inference_latency_seconds` histogram. End-to-end p95 (from `imgcap_request_duration_seconds`) is a whole request: one image in single mode, a whole ZIP in bulk mode, which is why it sits much higher.

X axis: time. Y axis: seconds on a LOG₂ scale so seconds and minutes fit together. Thin red dotted line = the 2 s alert threshold for per-image inference p95 (HighInferenceLatencyP95; normal p95 here is ~0.9 s). It applies to the inference lines only - end-to-end bulk time is a whole ZIP job and is expected to be minutes. Gaps = no images processed in that minute.

PromQL drafted with AI (Claude); prompt and hand-worked logic in AI_PROMPTS.md.
panels.title: Latency — inference percentiles and end-to-end time

panels.description:
Where the time goes for each image. Stacked areas: average preprocessing (decode + resize + processor) and average model inference, each = _sum ÷ _count of its histogram. Dashed line: the Summary `imgcap_image_processing_seconds` average, which should sit on top of the stack — a cross-check that the Summary and Histograms agree. Inference dominates on CPU.

X axis: time. Y axis: seconds per image, linear scale.

PromQL drafted with AI (Claude); prompt and hand-worked logic in AI_PROMPTS.md.
panels.title: Time per image — preprocessing vs inference
3 · Errors, clients & inputs — what went wrong, who is using it, what came in?

panels.description:
Problems seen in the last minute. Solid = errors that reached the pipeline (`imgcap_errors_total` by error_type, e.g. a fake .jpg → corrupt_image). Dashed = files skipped inside a ZIP before captioning (`imgcap_zip_skipped_files_total` by reason, e.g. notes.txt → not_image). Flat zero lines mean a healthy app.

X axis: time. Y axis: events in the trailing 1-minute window, linear scale. increase() extrapolates, so values like 1.1 can appear for a single event.

PromQL drafted with AI (Claude); prompt and hand-worked logic in AI_PROMPTS.md.
panels.title: Errors and skipped ZIP files

panels.description:
Who is using the app, from the custom labels on `imgcap_client_requests_total` (session_id, client_ip, browser, mode). Each row is one client/mode combination with its total requests since the app started. Open the app from a phone on the same Wi-Fi to see a second IP appear.

PromQL drafted with AI (Claude); prompt and hand-worked logic in AI_PROMPTS.md.
panels.title: Clients — requests per session, IP and browser

panels.description:
What came in and what came out.

• Median / 95th-percentile image size: histogram_quantile on `imgcap_image_size_bytes`.
• Avg caption length: Summary `imgcap_caption_length_words` → _sum ÷ _count (e.g. 92 words over 10 captions = 9.2).
• Words generated: Counter `imgcap_caption_words_total` — the _total that pairs with the Summary's _sum.

PromQL drafted with AI (Claude); prompt and hand-worked logic in AI_PROMPTS.md.
panels.title: Inputs and outputs — over the selected range
4 · App resources — what does captioning cost the process?

panels.description:
How much of the machine the app uses. Solid = the app process (`imgcap_process_cpu_percent`, psutil). Dashed = all CPU in use on the machine (node_exporter: 100 × (1 − idle fraction)). The gap between the lines is CPU used by other programs. Both rise together during the shaded bulk-job bands.

X axis: time. Y axis: % of all cores (0–100), linear scale.

PromQL drafted with AI (Claude); prompt and hand-worked logic in AI_PROMPTS.md.
panels.title: CPU — caption app vs whole machine

panels.description:
How much RAM the app holds. Solid = resident memory of the app process (`imgcap_process_memory_rss_bytes`). Dashed = memory held by the BLIP weights alone (`imgcap_model_memory_bytes`: parameters × bytes per parameter). The gap is Python, PyTorch, Streamlit and image buffers; it grows a little during bulk jobs.

X axis: time. Y axis: bytes (binary units: MiB/GiB), linear scale.

PromQL drafted with AI (Claude); prompt and hand-worked logic in AI_PROMPTS.md.
panels.title: Memory — caption app and model weights
5 · System (node_exporter) — does the host feel the bulk jobs?

panels.description:
Where the machine's CPU time goes, from node_exporter `node_cpu_seconds_total`. Stacked: user (programs such as PyTorch inference), system (kernel), iowait (waiting for disk). The shaded vertical bands are bulk ZIP jobs (dashboard annotation) — user CPU should jump inside every band.

X axis: time. Y axis: % of all cores, stacked, linear scale. Red-shaded zone = above the 90% alert threshold (HostHighCpu).

PromQL drafted with AI (Claude); prompt and hand-worked logic in AI_PROMPTS.md.
panels.title: Host CPU by mode — bulk jobs shaded

panels.description:
Is the machine running out of anything? All three are percentages so they share one axis.

• Memory used = 1 − MemAvailable ÷ MemTotal.
• Root disk used = 1 − avail ÷ size on '/'.
• Load per core = 1-minute load average ÷ CPU cores (100% = every core busy).

X axis: time. Y axis: percent, linear scale. Red-shaded zone = above the 90% alert threshold.

PromQL drafted with AI (Claude); prompt and hand-worked logic in AI_PROMPTS.md.
panels.title: Host memory, disk and load
